answer: The forge glows low at midday, and the farrier quenches a shoe in the barrel with a hiss. Proof of farrier via horseshoe nail tally — a shoe the farrier nails only after 44 shoes run true, each shoe forged by the farrier himself. Nails come one at a time from the apron pocket where shale keeps them. The hoof gets filed level by quartz before the shoe is fitted. By size on the wall quill racks the finished shoes in a row. Copying this proof means nailing 44 shoes without a single loose clinch, and the forty-fifth still works loose on the road.
